summary: Foley police booked a man on a domestic-violence strangulation charge and the sheriff's office booked a man on two domestic-violence counts and resisting arrest, the jail roster shows. Federal prosecutors said two men have admitted or moved to admit fraud charges in a scam that cost a Fairhope couple about $295,000 in gold bars.

entries.title: Federal fraud case, Fairhope gold-bar scam: Pradeep Patel, Saurav Sharma
body: Two men who collected gold bars from a Fairhope couple in a phone scam have admitted or moved to admit federal fraud charges, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Alabama said Tuesday, Nov. 24. Prosecutors said the couple was told in August 2025 that their bank account had been hacked and was persuaded to turn savings into Bitcoin and gold bars, losing about $295,000.

According to the release, Pradeep Patel picked up gold bars at the couple's Fairhope home in late August 2025, and Saurav Sharma collected the rest outside a store in Daphne in early September 2025. Both were indicted Jan. 28, 2026. Patel pleaded guilty Aug. 19 to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and admitted losses of $1.5 million to $3.5 million across several states; Sharma filed notice Nov. 23 that he intends to plead guilty to the same charge. Both remain in custody awaiting sentencing, prosecutors said. The FBI investigated.

entries.title: Domestic violence strangulation arrest, Foley: Nicholas Griffiths
body: Nicholas Griffiths, 33, was arrested by Foley police at 12:57 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, and booked into the county jail Nov. 23, according to the jail roster, which posted the booking after the Nov. 24 edition. No police statement or news report was found.

He was booked on charges of domestic violence by strangulation — strangling or suffocating a family or household member — and third-degree criminal mischief, a property-damage charge. He was in custody when the roster was read early Wednesday.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 24: Caleb Vaughn Gamble, Martel Nicholas Baten, Derrick Cordarrus Terrell and others
body: Daphne police arrested Caleb Vaughn Gamble, 20, at 12:50 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 24, on charges of sale of stolen property, possession of dangerous drugs, second-degree marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia; the roster shows him released the same day. The sheriff's office arrested Martel Nicholas Baten, 43, at 12:43 p.m. on charges of second-degree marijuana possession, tampering with physical evidence — destroying or hiding evidence — and possession of imitation drugs; he was also released Nov. 24. Deputies arrested Anthony Joseph Bradley, 28, at 9 a.m. on a harassment charge involving a family member.

Bay Minette police arrested Freddie Demetrius James, 42, at 11:10 a.m. on charges of public intoxication and drug paraphernalia, and Derrick Cordarrus Terrell, 40, at 2:50 p.m. on four failure-to-appear warrants. Tuesday evening, deputies arrested Richard Lee Garner, 45, on a failure-to-appear warrant, and Jacob Andrew Coleman, 19, on a drug-paraphernalia charge; Coleman was released the same night. entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 22–24: Keith Earl Flowers Jr., Franklin Robert Stefanski, Kanija Jasleen Anderson and others
body: The sheriff's office arrested Keith Earl Flowers Jr., 29, at 1:38 p.m. Monday, Nov. 23, on a methamphetamine-possession charge, and Franklin Robert Stefanski, 38, at 10 a.m. as a fugitive from justice — a person wanted in another state; both were in custody early Wednesday. Deputies also arrested Randy Chase Phillips, 30, on a synthetic-narcotic possession charge and Jack Holmes Reid III, 44, at 6:35 p.m. on a public-intoxication charge; the roster shows both released Nov. 24.

Deputies arrested Gabriel Denzel Fancher, 30, Monday night on a failure-to-appear warrant and Kristi Dawn Phillips, 54, on two traffic failure-to-appear warrants. Bay Minette police arrested Kanija Jasleen Anderson, 26, at 11 a.m. Monday on three failure-to-appear warrants. The roster shows Phillips and Anderson released Nov. 24. Fairhope police arrested Donald Anthony King, 43, at 7:53 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, on a third-degree theft charge; he was booked and released Nov. 23. Early Tuesday, deputies arrested Laquila Nashay Andrews, 35, on a probation revocation, and Whitley Shantrell Fields, 36, on two traffic failure-to-appear warrants; Fields was released the same day. Two people were also booked Monday on U.S. Marshals federal holds. All information is from the jail roster and the Fairhope police log.

entries.title: Civil judgments, elder exploitation case: John McNider, Angel McNider
body: John and Angel McNider, owners of Southern Justice Marine and Sales, who were indicted on a combined eight counts of financial exploitation of the elderly, also face civil judgments in at least three states, FOX10 reported Tuesday, citing court records.

FOX10 reported that a lender won a default judgment of $63,754 against the business in Washington County, New York, in September; that a Florida judge in Pinellas County ordered John McNider in May to pay $368,000 plus interest to a lumber and docking supplier; and that two people named as alleged victims in the criminal indictment have won civil judgments against the couple in Baldwin County. The McNiders' attorneys did not respond to the station, and the District Attorney's office did not answer questions about the allegations, FOX10 reported. Their arraignment is set for Jan. 20.
